purpose: What Acrevia cannot know from public zoning data alone. These entries are the honest boundary of this benchmark: UNKNOWN means the answer was not retrievable from authoritative public sources in this research pass; EXPERT_REQUIRED means the question needs professional or official judgment that Acrevia must not simulate.

questions.question: Title and deed review (OPA book/page 0880322): easements, restrictive covenants, denominational trust clauses, or disposition constraints on the parcel. OPA's owner string is an assessment record, not a title opinion.
questions.whyItMatters: A ground lease, sale, or development structure depends on unencumbered title; invisible covenants can prohibit residential use outright.

questions.question: Is the building or parcel listed on the Philadelphia Register of Historic Places? The local historic-district GIS layer shows no district here and the Landmark_Poly feature is a basemap label, but the Historical Commission's register was not queryable this session.
questions.whyItMatters: Register listing would add Historical Commission design review to any demolition or alteration scenario.

questions.question: Does the existing religious assembly use hold a special exception, or is it a legal nonconforming use? Requires permit-history research (L&I records / Zoning Archive).
questions.whyItMatters: Determines whether expanding or modifying the worship use triggers new approval, and what happens if the use lapses.

questions.question: Does Title 14 impose any floor-area-ratio regulation in RM-1? The official guide's Table 14-701-2 prints no FAR value for RM-1, and adopted-text capture of that table was blocked by the code host.
questions.whyItMatters: A solver must know whether FAR is a constraint class at all in this district.

questions.question: Do any geographic bonus restrictions apply to this parcel? The guide says 'For bonus restrictions in select geographic areas, see page 49', but the printed page 49 contains no such list — the pointer could not be resolved within the guide.
questions.whyItMatters: The 25%/50% mixed-income unit bonuses may be unavailable in restricted areas; assuming they apply could overstate capacity.

questions.question: How many off-street parking spaces exist today, and what is Sunday utilization? The church's website does not mention a parking lot; no public source inventories stalls.
questions.whyItMatters: Any mission constraint like 'keep Sunday parking' needs a baseline count; zoning requires 0 spaces for new multi-family, so parking retention would be a mission choice, not a code minimum.

questions.question: Sanctuary seat count (worship parking ratio is 1 per 10 seats or 1 per 1,000 sq ft, whichever is greater).
questions.whyItMatters: Required parking for the continuing worship use scales with seats; unknown until surveyed.

questions.question: Phase I Environmental Site Assessment for the portion of the parcel not covered by the mapped building footprint (potential fill, tanks, historic uses) has not been performed.
questions.whyItMatters: Environmental conditions can determine buildability and cost more than zoning does.

questions.question: Curb-cut / driveway permits and access control along the Roosevelt Boulevard frontage; which agency's jurisdiction applies (city Streets Department vs state) was not verified.
questions.whyItMatters: Access points constrain site layout; boulevard frontage may have dedicated-access rules.

questions.question: Water, sewer, and electric capacity for significant new development on this block.
questions.whyItMatters: Utility capacity is a classic silent feasibility constraint invisible in zoning data.

questions.question: Overlay identification used a centroid point-intersect. A polygon-level sweep across the full parcel boundary for edge-touching overlays was not run for the overlay layer (it WAS run for buildings).
questions.whyItMatters: An overlay crossing only a parcel corner could be missed by a centroid test.

questions.question: Zoning layers reported pending 'No' at retrieval, and the code host notes its text may lag recent legislation. Councilmatic rezoning activity after 2026-10-04 is outside this benchmark.
questions.whyItMatters: Zoning can change; this is the Watch issue's (#17) re-verification responsibility, and any real submission must re-check.

questions.question: The congregation's actual priorities (preserve sanctuary? keep the school? retain parking? ownership structure? income goals?) have not been gathered.
questions.whyItMatters: Mission constraints are first-class solver inputs in Acrevia; they must come from the church, not be invented. Feeds issues #6 and #20.

questions.question: Exact layout, surfacing, tree cover, and drainage of the ~74% of the parcel not covered by the mapped building footprint; no imagery analysis or survey was performed.
questions.whyItMatters: Usable-area and placement logic depend on real site conditions.
